advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Share ONE definition of 'disposition with a live replacement' between transition_close and close_disposition (have the guard reuse find_replacement, or vice versa) so the guard and the signing-verdict cannot disagree.
evidence: close_disposition.py:26 `def find_replacement(ticket_id: str, close_class: str, tracker: str) -> str | None:` — body mirrors transition_close.py:104-146 `_has_live_replacement_link` (same duplicates-dep scan then supersedes inbound scan)

transition_close.py:259-265 `if _has_live_replacement_link(...): ... return close_disposition.verdict(ticket_id, close_class, tracker)` — guard and re-derivation are two independent reads of the same graph

close_disposition.py:64-66 both use `except Exception: return None` fail-closed, so a transient store read that succeeds in the guard but fails in find_replacement yields verdict()->None -> unsigned close

The only drift protection is tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:26 `assert close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES == transition_close._NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` — it pins the class sets but NOT that find_replacement and _has_live_replacement_link agree on which links qualify
Ticket 738a AC #2 asked that the two halves 'share ONE definition of "disposition with a live replacement"' — the implementation instead duplicated it
advisory.finding: find_replacement() in close_disposition.py duplicates the replacement-resolution logic of transition_close._has_live_replacement_link almost verbatim, but the two are exercised as a guard/re-derive pair on the SAME close path: _completion_precheck requires _has_live_replacement_link()==True, then calls close_disposition.verdict() which re-derives via find_replacement(). If the two ever diverge (or a transient read fails between them), the guard passes True while find_replacement returns None, so verdict() returns None and the disposition close lands UNSIGNED — silently reproducing the exact bug 738a fixes. Only the class-SET equality is pinned by a test, not the resolution logic.
advisory.suggested_fix: Make _has_live_replacement_link delegate to close_disposition.find_replacement (return find_replacement(...) is not None), or have _completion_precheck compute the replacement once and pass it into verdict(), eliminating the second independent read.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the dead `transition_close.gates`/hasattr monkeypatch block in the force-close test and keep only the effective `_gates.gate_enabled` patch.
evidence: test file:62-67 `monkeypatch.setattr(transition_close.gates if hasattr(transition_close, 'gates') else transition_close, 'gate_enabled', lambda *a, **k: True, raising=False)`

transition_close.py:225 `from rebar._commands import gates` — imported lazily inside _completion_precheck, so `transition_close.gates` does not exist at module scope and the ternary falls to patching the module itself
test file:68-70 `from rebar._commands import gates as _gates` then `monkeypatch.setattr(_gates, 'gate_enabled', lambda *a, **k: True)` — this is the patch that actually takes effect
advisory.finding: The force-close ordering test primes the disposition path with a confused/dead monkeypatch: it patches `transition_close.gates if hasattr(transition_close, 'gates') else transition_close` with attribute 'gate_enabled', but transition_close imports `gates` lazily inside _completion_precheck and does not hold a module-level `gates` attribute, so that setattr targets the transition_close module with an unused attribute. Only the subsequent `monkeypatch.setattr(_gates, 'gate_enabled', ...)` is load-bearing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that exercises find_replacement against a real tracker with a live 'duplicates' target and a real inbound 'supersedes' source, asserting the correct replacement id is returned and that a dead/archived target yields None.
evidence: test_every_exempt_class_can_produce_a_verdict monkeypatches the unit under test: `monkeypatch.setattr(close_disposition, "find_replacement", lambda *a, **k: "dead-beef-cafe-0001")`

Both real find_replacement calls use a nonexistent tracker: line 42 `close_disposition.verdict("tkt-0001", close_class, "/nonexistent/tracker")` and line 111 `close_disposition.find_replacement("tkt-0001", close_class, "/nonexistent/tracker")`, both exercising only the None/fail-closed path

close_disposition.py:63-89 (find_replacement) contains the untested logic: `if dep.get("relation") != "duplicates"` / `target = str(dep.get("target_id", dep.get("target", "")))` / inbound `link.get("relation") != "supersedes"` / `_is_live_ticket(...)` — none of these branches is reached with a positive result by any test
ABSENCE: a regression returning the wrong replacement id, matching the wrong link direction, or skipping the liveness check would still name an id in the signed manifest and pass all current tests
advisory.finding: The positive path of close_disposition.find_replacement — the directional link resolution (outbound 'duplicates' dep, inbound 'supersedes' link, the target_id/target fallback) and the _is_live_ticket liveness gate — has no test coverage. The only happy-path verdict test monkeypatches find_replacement itself, and every real call passes '/nonexistent/tracker' which returns None via the fail-closed except before any traversal runs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add cases building a real rebar repo (as tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_link_exemptions.py does) that link a live canonical/duplicate and assert find_replacement returns that id, plus an archived-target case asserting None — instead of monkeypatching find_replacement in the verdict test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end test that closes a linked-duplicate bug and asserts the closure carries a valid completion-verifier attestation (and that its parent's certification is no longer withheld).
evidence: The diff's stated fix: 'A disposition close now MINTS an attestation ... A signature claiming a PASS would be a lie in the signed bytes' — the observable regression is 'unsigned closure -> now signed/certified'

transition_close.py:259-265: the wired call `return close_disposition.verdict(ticket_id, close_class, tracker)` replacing the old `return None`; no test drives _completion_precheck through this branch to a real signed closure (the force-close test deliberately stops at the guard and mocks verdict away)

Nearest existing coverage tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_link_exemptions.py:52-61 asserts only `calls == []` and `_status(bug) == "closed"` — it does NOT assert the closure is now signed or that certification is no longer withheld
ABSENCE: if the wiring in _completion_precheck or _verdict_manifest silently regressed to leaving the close unsigned, no test would fail
advisory.finding: No test asserts the end-to-end behavior the fix delivers: that a disposition close now produces a SIGNED completion-verifier attestation (previously it was unsigned and counted UNCERTIFIED by child_closure_findings). The unit tests stop at verdict()/decorate_manifest() return values; the regression that 738a fixes — an unsigned exempt child withholding the parent's signature — is not covered.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the lifecycle exemption test (or add a sibling) to assert that after the disposition close the ticket has a signed completion-verifier record whose kind is 'completion-verifier' and whose manifest first line is 'completion-verifier: DISPOSITION <class>'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-validate the disposition's live-replacement link on read (in compute_validity or child_closure_findings) so a disposition attestation is invalidated when its replacement link is removed or its replacement ticket is no longer live — not only at mint time.
evidence: close_disposition.verdict mints the sign signal only after find_replacement succeeds: 'replacement = find_replacement(ticket_id, close_class, tracker); if replacement is None: return None' (close_disposition.py:100-102)
The mint-time check reads the live link: find_replacement iterates state['deps'] for relation=='duplicates' and inbound 'supersedes', gated by _is_live_ticket (close_disposition.py:69-88)

Read-side validity does NOT re-check the replacement: compute_validity for kind=='completion-verifier' returns 'certified' after only (a) status=='closed' and (b) material fingerprint match — 'return {"valid": True, ..., "verdict": "certified"}' (attest.py:661-685)

The material fingerprint basis is ticket_id/description/file_impact/children only — the duplicates/supersedes relation is NOT included, and children are parent-child links: basis = {'ticket_id', 'description', 'file_impact', 'children'} (pass1.py:761-768); docstring: 'Tags/comments/links/assignee are NOT material (excluded)' (pass1.py:752-753)

child_closure_findings treats any certified+valid completion-verifier attestation as certification, forwarding to the parent: 'if sig.get("verdict") == "certified": ... valid, detail = v.get("valid", False), ...' (completion.py:172-177)

The ticket comment FIXED-738A-B claims the material step makes validity 'identical semantics to a verified completion, not a permanently-valid special case' — but material never covers the replacement link, so the claimed safeguard does not protect the disposition's actual basis.
advisory.finding: A disposition attestation's justifying invariant — a LIVE replacement link — is verified only at mint time (find_replacement), but is never re-checked on read: compute_validity for 'completion-verifier' checks only status=='closed' and this ticket's material fingerprint, and the material fingerprint does not include the duplicates/supersedes dependency link or the replacement's liveness. Removing the link or deleting/archiving the replacement leaves the disposition attestation permanently 'certified', and child_closure_findings then forwards that certification to the parent.
scenarios: A bug is closed --class duplicate against a live replacement, minting a certified completion-verifier attestation without any verification; the duplicates link is later edited away (or the replacement ticket is deleted/archived). The attestation remains 'certified' and the parent epic certifies over a child whose exemption basis no longer holds.

An operator or automation removes/retargets the replacement relationship after close; validity-on-read does not detect it, so an unattested-in-substance subtree keeps propagating certification upward.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the completion-verifier validity path (or child_closure_findings), when an attestation's manifest[0] is 'completion-verifier: DISPOSITION <class>', re-run the live-replacement predicate (share close_disposition.find_replacement / transition_close._has_live_replacement_link) and treat the attestation as invalid/uncertified when the replacement link is no longer net-active or the replacement is no longer a live ticket.
